answer: A staked-identity registry prices each identity by a locked bond. A Sybil attack becomes an inventory problem: N clones cost N minimum stakes, and any clone caught colluding forfeits its pledge. Rewards track verified work, roughly linear per account, while capital at risk scales with identity count, so duplicating yourself never lifts yield per locked unit. Each voice needs its own reef of verified history and a cedar-hard committed balance that cannot be copied; records stay ferrous across epochs, so clones cannot inherit reputation. Ten thousand voices means ten thousand forfeitable stakes.
